nodes.summary: There exist a field $k$, a finite group $G$ and a faithful absolutely irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ such that the first cohomology group $H^1(G, V)$ has dimension greater than $2$ over $k$.
nodes.title: Mazurov's question on first cohomology (Kourovka 16.55) has a negative answer

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every field $k$, every finite group $G$ and every faithful absolutely irreducible representation $\rho$ of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, the first cohomology group $H^1(G, V)$ has dimension at most $2$ over $k$.
nodes.title: Mazurov's question on first cohomology (Kourovka 16.55)

nodes.summary: A representation $\rho$ of a group $G$ on a vector space $V$ over a field $k$ is absolutely irreducible when $V \neq 0$, the only $G$-invariant subspaces of $V$ are $0$ and $V$, and every $k$-linear endomorphism of $V$ commuting with $\rho(g)$ for all $g \in G$ is a scalar multiple of the identity.
nodes.title: Absolutely irreducible representations
